items.title: uv sync --only-group and --no-extra still evaluates other package sources not specified, source = path
items.reason: Closest canonical match: sync evaluates an unavailable path source from a non-selected group or extra. Maintainers explain that all groups are resolved and recommend frozen mode when using an existing lockfile.

items.title: uv requires platform-specific wheels to be present, even on different platforms
items.reason: Exact precedent for locked mode inspecting an unavailable platform-specific path distribution. Maintainers confirmed that locked mode resolves to validate the lockfile and recommended frozen mode.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests using the exact errors and identifiers (`Distribution not found at`, `Failed to generate package metadata`, `--no-group`, `--no-sources-package`, dependency metadata and hashes), plus conceptual terms covering excluded groups, unavailable path/private sources, cross-platform distributions, lockfile validation, and frozen mode. No closer pull request was found. astral-sh/uv#9804 was redundant with the selected matches; astral-sh/uv#11104 concerns inaccessible private indexes; astral-sh/uv#13487 concerns cross-platform locking without group selection; and astral-sh/uv#21429 retains the missing path as a selected direct dependency.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#11675 already tracks the same underlying behavior: sync resolves a path source even when its group or extra is excluded from installation. The `--locked` condition does not establish a regression because current documentation and astral-sh/uv#11573 confirm that locked mode performs resolution to validate the lockfile.
summary: astral-sh/uv#11675 is the closest open discussion, while astral-sh/uv#11573 confirms the exact locked-versus-frozen behavior for unavailable path distributions.
draft_response:
Thanks for the report. This matches astral-sh/uv#11675. `--no-group lab` excludes that group from the environment sync, but not from the resolution used to validate the lockfile. Since `--locked` asserts that the lockfile would remain unchanged after resolution, uv still inspects the declared path source. `--no-sources-package smaract-ctl` changes the source used for that resolution rather than removing the group, which is why uv then searches the registry.

When the lockfile was generated where the archive is available, use `uv sync --frozen --no-group lab --no-progress` on machines where it is unavailable. `--frozen` uses the existing lockfile without validating it through another resolution, so dependency metadata should not be necessary. Let's keep the broader discussion in astral-sh/uv#11675.
